title: Atomic OCI index rotation + kernel preflight checks for air-gapped upgrades
author: Priya Nambiar
release_notes: Adds an atomic OCI index rotation cli, host preflight kernel checks, and registry seed/rotation hooks for safe airgapped upgrades. Backwards compatible with existing seed bundles.
description:
Motivation:
Air-gapped upgrades require a predictable, atomic promotion of OCI artifacts and a robust host preflight to avoid subtle kernel/runtime incompatibilities. Customers previously observed mid-upgrade failures when a node lacked required kernel config (overlayfs, cgroup v2 settings) or when the registry promotion left a brief window of inconsistent index state. This PR introduces two coordinated capabilities: 1) a catalog-rotate command that atomically promotes a signed OCI index and staged blob set into the customer registry, and 2) a small preflight binary run by the installer that validates host kernel and iptables/ebtables variants before upgrading.

What I changed (high level):
- new CLI subcommand `installer catalog-rotate --staged-index INDEX.json --target-registry REG` that: verifies signatures, computes an atomic index manifest with pinned digests, uploads a single index manifest and then flips a lightweight pointer tag; on registries that support OCI redirects we use a two-phase rename to avoid index inconsistencies.
- added host preflight binary `redwood-preflight` (Go, static) which checks: overlayfs availability, CONFIG_NAMESPACES and cgroup-controller availability, required sysctls (net.ipv4.ip_forward, vm.max_map_count), container runtime socket reachability, and iptables vs nft compatibility. The binary emits machine-readable JSON and exit codes that the installer uses to decide to abort or warn.
- installer hooks for airgap: `seed/rotate` terraform/helm helpers that pre-seed the registry with staged blobs and expose a `rotate` operation that the catalog-rotate command calls as the final step.
- helm chart tweak: make image references immutable by default and add an annotation `redwood.io/catalog-pinned: "true"` used by the rotate step.
- metadata: added `distro-matrix.json` to the offline bundle schema that declares kernel capability gates for each distro+kernel-min version. The preflight reads this file when present.

Checklist:
- [x] CLI: catalog-rotate implementation + unit tests
- [x] preflight binary + integration tests in local VM matrix
- [x] terraform helpers to seed registries in CI smoke harness
- [x] Helm chart annotation and README upgrade note
- [x] Offline-bundle metadata bump + example distro-matrix.json
- [x] Docs: installer/airgap upgrade guide section updated

Upgrade/rollback notes:
- Rotation is atomic from the consumer point-of-view: we upload the final pinned index and then update the pointer tag. If a rotation fails, the existing pointer tag remains untouched. The rotate tool records a rotation journal entry under `/var/lib/redwood/registry-rotate/journal` so the installer can automatically roll back a partially-seeded rotate by replacing the pointer with the previous manifest.
- Preflight failures prevent an automated upgrade and surface clear remediation steps. For advanced users the installer supports `--force-unsafe-upgrade` but this toggles out of the safety SLA and will require signed acceptance.

Testing performed: 
- unit tests for index mutation and signature verification (Go test).
- multi-distro VM matrix (Ubuntu20.04, Rocky9, Photon4) exercising kernel gating paths.
- CI job `airgap-smoke` that runs the terraform registry seed flow against a local registry and executes `catalog-rotate` to verify no lost manifests. This job was re-run twice after flaky network tests were fixed.

Security considerations:
- `catalog-rotate` validates the signed index before promotion and rejects any unsigned or mismatched blob sets. Keys are validated against the bundle's signer public key.
- The journal is owned by root and has strict perms. The rotate flow does not expose any control-plane endpoints over the network; registry operations are executed by the client with pre-provisioned credentials.

Backwards compatibility:
- Existing offline bundles continue to work. If `distro-matrix.json` is not present the preflight uses conservative default checks. The rotate command is opt-in; existing customers can continue using the current seed + manual promotion flow.

Related work: ENG-2143 (airgap upgrade reliability), SEC-98 (offline catalog signing), SUP-312 (customer reported failed upgrade due to overlayfs bug).

review_comments: Evan Morris: Nice work — the two-phase flip makes sense. Can we add a small timeout/guard for registries that don't support tag mutations?
Priya Nambiar: Added a 30s guard and a fallback that writes the pointer via a signed ref manifest. Documented the compatibility section in README.
Lina Gomez: The preflight binary is great; please ensure we don't require cgroup v2 for customers on older distros. Could you add matrix exceptions?

Priya Nambiar: The distro-matrix.json supports explicit exceptions; preflight will only fail if the distro entry marks the capability as required. Defaults are conservative to avoid accidental failures.
Arjun Patel: CI smoke flaked once due to the local registry TLS certs. You resolved it by pinning a self-signed cert in the job — ok to merge once green.
Priya Nambiar: Correct — CI now bootstraps a local registry with the test cert and the job includes the cert bundle upload step.
